name: Rhône Valley
keyfacts: In the northern Rhône crus, Syrah is the only red grape, sometimes with a little white grape, and the whites come from Marsanne, Roussanne and Viognier.
The northern Rhône has a temperate continental climate, and the mistral, a cold, dry and often violent north wind, sweeps the valley.
In Châteauneuf-du-Pape, rounded pebbles store the sun's heat by day and release it at night, helping the grapes ripen fully.

notes: Northern Rhône reds, from Syrah, are known for aromas of green olive and smoky bacon.
Southern reds from the left bank are full bodied and tannic when young, with aromas of prune, undergrowth, chocolate and ripe black fruit.
Right bank reds are slightly lighter and fruitier.

blurb.text: A wine region of France divided into the Northern Rhône and the Southern Rhône. Its appellations include Cairanne, Vinsobres and Costières de Nîmes.
